reviews.text: Superhero Simulator is hands down the most refreshing and entertaining game I’ve played in years. Forget the endless grind of games like GTA V Online or the repetitive missions of Marvel’s Avengers—this game actually understands what being a superhero AND a human is all about. One moment you’re saving the city from villains in an epic showdown, and the next you’re flipping pancakes in your tiny apartment, worrying about rent. It’s funny, it’s deep, and it’s strangely relatable. Unlike so many AAA titles that drown in microtransactions and soulless content, Superhero Simulator delivers pure joy and originality. Honestly, this is the game Marvel’s Avengers should have been. I can’t recommend it enough!

Most "simulator" games don't really do their professions justice. As an actual superhero I can say this is a perfect recreation of my day. It is so hard trying to balance my paycheck with my hero duties and it seems like I can barely even take a break going to the bathroom. If you want to see what it's like to be a superhero try this game out. If you like it maybe becoming a superhero is for you as well.

have a lot of potential! I can't wait to see more update to fix bugs add more boss, more hideout plus custom hideout, more suit, more jobs, more super abilities... Imagine if this game and No Man's Sky have a baby! We would have a superman game take place in the whole universe. I wish some one good enough and rich enough to see this idea and make it actually happen.

I've been excited about this game for a while and was disappointed today when I downloaded it. Many parts of the game are clearly AI (Voice acting, music, billboard art...) yet this was disclosed to me before I made my purchase. This game makes you feel more like an anti-hero. I imagined I would be like Super-Man, but this game felt more like a cruel parody of what we imagine superheroes to be. The citizens are cruel to you if you save them. They're snarky and seem to follow a 'random is funny' format. It was enjoyable for the first few times I heard it, but it got old REALLY fast. I don't want to be cursed at or insulted by everyone I save- let alone the lady on the radio. Missions come up very quickly once you're out of the tutorial. You physically have no time to reach them all, and are taunted by the lady on the radio for 'letting a criminal escape' or whatnot. No matter how hard you try, people WILL die and they will die OFTEN and it will be YOUR fault. The taxi job is frustrating as well. The game does not give you enough time to drive safely through the city. You HAVE to be reckless, speeding and driving up onto sidewalks all at over 70 MPH in order to make it to the checkpoint in time. I understand this may be alright for games like GTA. But this is a superhero simulator, a game where you're simulating as a good person doing good things. I don't feel like I'm doing good things in this game. This game clearly has potential but it is simply not being handled correctly at the moment. Remove the generative AI, adjust the missions to be POSSIBLE, make interactions feel more realistic (and NOT a cruel parody)- then I will be interested in this game again. It was SO fun to fly around and fight villains and put out fires but everything I've mentioned really brought the hype down. I tried to ignore it but I couldn't. As always, this is just constructive criticism, so don't take it as an insult. The comic-like art style is cool, unique, and beautiful. It was just overshadowed by these problems.

Core gameplay is bad "Every hero has walked away, but chaos never did" said the trailer. Well..... no wonder they walked away. As much as I want to like the game... it's still a bad game. The city itself aint functioning at all. The believability just got killed once the game let you do the freeroaming. first of all, I do understand the vibe they're going with the game, endless work, thankless job and such, the sup works you have to do here are a bunch of mini games, but after five minutes you started to realize "There is zero emergency service working in the town" No cop, no fire department, no emergency transporter of any kind. a building is on fire => wait for the hero a man getting drowned=> wait for the hero gang violence=> wait for the hero having a heart attack=> wait for the hero a bomb getting planted=> wait for the hero hostage situation => wait for the hero a kid got lost=> you guess it, wait for 1 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hero.... oh and this one is the worst. a typically dumb mom forgot her child somewhere and asked you to find the kid, there're 4 potential "children" marked on the map which you never know which one is hers, you only get 3 chances... each time you guess it wrong, the mom will smack you on the head and insult you to oblivion!! "that was obviously a grown man" she said... well I would have known IF YOU USED A DIFFERENT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MODEL!! and of course the time will inevitably run out for each event, you can't do them all..... it's all fine... until you hear the insult from emergency operators smacking you for every single accident you missed while you were busy saving lives, instead of.... I don't know, do your own damn job providing the victims with corresponding services accordingly!! Progression is BS The progressions you gained from leveling up completing jobs are quite useless, at least the early on.... what is the point of jumping higher when you can fly from the start? what is the point of dashing when the only scenario needed for you to fight is gang violent where 6 men standing still shooting at you occasionally and you can press "E" to perform a preemptive strike instead of dodging and wasting even more time to run back to the scene [time is important, mind you, because missing events costs you peace meter] Here's how to fix the game initially.... *implement emergency services* get rid of smacking complaints from the operators or lower the rate to 5-10% I could go on and on about other aspects of the game... but typing is tiring nowadays. PS.for the love of gods, fix that abomination missing child quest at this stage, this game is worth a buy only if you're into masochistic side and love hearing ♥♥♥♥ talking

有些失望，第一次玩游戏的Demo感觉玩法还是挺有意思的，主角作为英雄和普通人的双重身份被游戏灌入了玩法中，既可以当英雄飞天遁地，又可以当凡人体验普通人的生活，但是游戏任务的布置太过紧凑一个任务还没做完，另一个任务就结束了，每次游玩下来就跟催命似的难受，正反馈与负反馈难以平衡，希望制作组把开始任务的方法给到玩家，由玩家自主选择承接哪个任务，而不是这个任务在一定时间内没去做就会自动消除还会扣分。 然而在玩家好不容易结束了当超人时不良好的游戏体验后，还得去当凡人承接各种人物去赚钱，当普通人赚钱没什么不好，毕竟也是该游戏玩法的一部分，但是在赚钱的途中和平等级会一点一点流失，这不免让玩家思考，我这么累的玩这个游戏是为什么，我可是个超级英雄，不想要再体验正常生活有多么的辛苦，希望制作组能够重视玩家的游玩体验 虽然我对这个游戏失望，但还是会给予该游戏好评，市面上超人游戏实在少之又少难以找到此类大型游戏，所以我仍然要感谢制作组给我带来这款作品
Its honestly a pretty solid game, pretty impressive considering it was only made by 7 people. look forward to more updates,well done guys and gals!!

Games like this is why Im learning to program. I already have 3d character art skills but I need to learn to program to make my own games. This game is a game I've wanted to make all my life, a game that highlights the double life of a superhero but it isn't perfect. As an artist I wouldn't be comfortable using AI, these devs are. I would also wait until I had more than one power set to release the game but that's just me. This game is more "Superman Simulator" or "Invincible Simulator" than it is "Superhero Simulator" because of the fact that theres only one kind of character you can be at the moment. It's also janky, the AI voices are annoying and theres barely any content but as someone who has wanted to make this game, or even see this kind of thing made and succeed, I felt the call to support these developers in their endeavor. If you don't want to simply support more superhero games being made, then maybe wait a year or so and see if this thing is worth it then. At the moment I would say for most people, it won't be worth it, its barely worth it for me and superheroes, comics, etc are my favorite thing media wise. I will watch this games progress over the next year and see if theres anything to change in this review then, until then, I cannot in good faith recommend this game as it stands. I love the idea, I don't love the execution so far.

the first time i’m writing a review of this length simply because i see developers actively engaging with the community, which to me is always a plus. i see the word “potential” thrown around when talking about this game, because ultimately you can tell it’s nowhere near finished, and while i’m grateful for the devs giving us early access i think most of the criticism is valid. excessive ai content, no girl model at launch (that rlly sucks), repetitive content, etc. however for a somewhat casual player, just putting on my own music while flying around the city fighting crime and making a silly character is enough for me, especially for a $10 experience where there is seemingly no other game of this style out there. some things i’d like to see personally would be more things to do as your non-hero persona, whether that be just to walk around the city, or maybe even a stardew like approach where there are characters that you can build relationships with, and having that balance between your normal life and superhero life could add more depth. maybe a deeper more interesting villain system that is more immersive and personal. a girl character that won’t take a year to make…please… there are lots of directions they could take which makes me excited for them as they clearly seem to care about what they’re making. and i obviously can’t tell you what to do but please for the love of god…put down the ai. there are plenty of talented people that i’m sure would be thrilled to design art and do voice lines. you guys have something that could be very special, just put in the effort :)

[h1]简介[/h1] 《Superhero Simulator》超人模拟器，顾名思义这是一款以扮演超能力者为主的游戏，游戏的起因就是我们扮演的角色内分泌失调同时也获得了梦寐以求的上天入地的超能力。但有了这一身能力后，角色的生活是否能发生变化？是否能改变自身的生活环境，至少这款游戏是给了一些思路和设想，还挺有意思的。 [h1]超人？明明是阿祖[/h1] 游戏的特色很明显，超人强不强首先就看能不能飞。所以首先就是地图城市的质量，相较于同时突变超能力的蜘蛛侠，本作也有一个还算大的城市。不过城市应该是某种算法生成的，看着有点千篇一律，不过都这个价位了还要什么自行车。同时游戏的玩法也分为战斗和生活，战斗就是和蜘蛛侠一样，会在地图上标记出有犯罪的地方，这是我们可以操作超人直接到达现场，惩奸除恶。生活嘛，皮特帕克不也是租房子吗，所以除了打击犯罪，还有一个就是生活玩法，赚钱。而这里的赚钱也很有意思，居然是开出租车。 不过在这方面的设计，应该是鼓励玩家不要循规蹈矩，因为正常开车的出租时间非常的紧张，而且都有超能力了还会因为钱而发愁，嗯怎么说呢，文化差异吧。 但老实说战斗的玩法也不是很好，主要还是那个问题，我都是超人了，战斗还要循规蹈矩的，真的有点说不通了，因为本作有一个还算爽的玩法。 那就是城市破坏啦，终于可以像阿祖那样不受约束的爽爽了，可惜作为唯一爽的要素，玩起来也就几分钟的热度就觉得无聊了。所以在感觉到无聊前，一定要多破坏点大楼，而且还专门有一个城市破坏度这个设定。整个游戏玩下来就这个最好玩。 [h1]总结[/h1] 总的来说，这是一款优缺点并存的游戏，结合售价，结合玩法，还要什么自行车。只是战斗玩法和生活玩法简直是多余，为啥挣钱一定要开出租车，都能飞了送外卖不好吗，而且都当超人了不知道的还以为是出租车模拟器。唯一好玩的城市破坏，讲真，真的没几个游戏作这种玩法的，第一次玩新奇满满，大楼破坏加爆炸，爽快的不要不要的。如果能多深挖一下这方面的玩法，肯定要比开出租车挣钱和聊胜于无的战斗强太多。如果想玩一个不一样的超人游戏，那么本作就是，至少开始妥妥的一个阿祖模拟器，但回归到生活了，就又开始变的无趣，按需选择吧。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

站在你面前的是一位光头猛男，他叫超人，但又非一个正常的超人，他其实是个没工作的穷逼。《 Superhero Simulator》是一款超人模拟器游戏，你将扮演超人，但同时也要为生活奔波，忙于生计，太真实了吧我的哥。 [h1]本来以为是超人，结果没想到是祖国人[/h1] 作为一个名义上的超人，钢铁之躯、超高速飞行这些都是你的身体优势。游戏开局只有简单的肤色选择，甚至连性别都不能选。你的室友是一个被赶出家门的肥仔，在他自诩你的后援后，便开始指挥你做事，如出门打击犯罪，拯救市民。 但是我在游玩过程中发现，高速飞行可以撞坏大楼，于是便开始肆无忌惮的破坏。除此之外，游戏比较难绷的一点就是，超人明明有钢铁之躯，打小怪还不能一拳一个，虽然血不会掉，但是打得费劲，落差感太强了，实战效果应该是一拳打飞一个敌人才对。鉴于这些做好事的行为收益太低且正反馈不足，我就开始安心当祖国人，在城市肆意破坏，即使城市安全系数下降也无所谓，因为游戏根本没有做相关的内容，系数下降到一的时候就再无可降了。 [h1]不会开出租车的超人不是个好厨子[/h1] 超人虽然身体上已经无敌于世间，按理说不应该为生活发愁，但是本作确实是这样。男主穷的叮当响，甚至还亏欠房租。无可奈何的他只好出门找工作，当出租车司机，开得不好还会被愤怒的乘客竖中指，这个时候就可以开车直接碾压他们，当什么超人，我要当祖国人！此外，超人还会去餐厅当厨子，给客人烹饪美食。超人也是一个人，能量、卫生、精力这些数值都要时刻保持，吃饭、洗澡、上厕所都能恢复这些数值。 [h1]最大的优点是换装系统[/h1] 男主开头是个光头，而且也没有什么正式衣服，只有一件随意换色的超人服。值得一提的是，超人服能幻化成很多熟悉的角色，如黑蜘蛛侠、一拳超人等形象，搞怪风格浓郁，后面还可以去理发店理发。到最后，超人可以是任意形象，只取决于你的想法。 [h1]结语[/h1] 游戏目前有很多不足，亟待修改，如战斗系统拉跨，打击手感不足等；此外，游戏的色彩饱和度太高，看久了容易视觉疲劳；最后建议在城市安全系数这块可以做点修改，比如下降到 0 会发生什么，或者能不能给超人一个真正黑化成祖国人的选项，能肆意破坏城市显然比当社畜要爽。游戏目前还处于 ea 阶段，有些许问题在所难免，这是一款值得期待的作品，可以一试！ [quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]

[quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote] [h1]《超级英雄模拟器》：生活模拟类的“超人”版蜘蛛侠[/h1] 虽然《Superhero Simulator》对标的并不是诸如《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆骑士》和《漫威蜘蛛侠》这样的超级英雄大作，而是市面上各种流行泛滥的低成本、小体量、高乐趣的模拟类游戏，因此它的游戏体验相比之下可能有些略显单薄。但就这类游戏而言，更加有趣的题材和可以更加无脑的模拟玩法，也让这款另辟蹊径的作品成为了一款更加有趣的模拟游戏。 在内容上，为了玩法的醋而包了一盘饺子的《超级英雄模拟器》套用了一层非常无脑的超级英雄背景设定，只不过比那些剧情向的超级英雄游戏更加生活化也更贴合模拟主题的是，玩家作为一个从外星降临的超人系光头超级英雄，除了打击犯罪，还需要打工赚钱支付房租，因此游戏的整体设定更像是一个套用了托比版彼得·帕克背景故事的超人。 而作为一款超级英雄题材的生活模拟类游戏，本作的玩法基本上可以分为三个大种类，即属于超级英雄生涯的打击犯罪与帮助平民，以及包含打工日常在内的生活模拟。 其中，前两者需要你在利用超人的游戏性能探索地图的过程中解决随机刷新在城市中的各种灾难以及犯罪事件，比如罪犯当街袭击、超级罪犯挑衅、大楼着火、船只失事平民落水、平民被砸在废墟下、病人需要急救等随机事件。严格来说，本作的开放世界游戏设计其实相当于是将《漫威蜘蛛侠》里的主线剧情删除、只剩下开放世界随机犯罪与无剧情的好邻居支线以后的结果。 而且在游戏性能上，本作并没有像以往的各种标题党的仿蜘蛛侠手游一样去模仿蜘蛛侠或是设计一个相对来说比较原创的超级英雄形象，而是选择了更为无脑更好还原且市面上几乎没有什么同类作品的超人类超级英雄当做模板，除了只能提现在具体任务里的超级力量以外，玩家可以实现高速飞行、用嘴灭火等技能，因此在玩家操作以及制作人的游戏设计上都可以做到相对无脑，其实也降低了不少玩家的操作压力。 当然，在游戏模式上，就和大部分模拟游戏一样，当你在开放世界进行探索时，地图上会不停地刷新出随机事件，然而，这些事件持续时间都不算很长，且距离较远，而且你还要同时兼顾主角的体力值，否则如果你因为耗尽体力继续行动而倒下，就会被扣除医药费后在医院醒来。 因此，作为模拟游戏，本作倒是也像其他模拟作品那样做出了一种手忙脚乱的感觉。但就模拟游戏来说，本作的题材还是依旧非常有趣的。

这是一款超人模拟器游戏。 游戏的画面是美漫渲染风格，略微有点无主之地那个味的，有一个比较大的城市地图，不过城市的建筑千篇一律，虽然也有小人和车辆在城市里移动，但是总体来说画面还是比较粗糙的。 设定就是玩家扮演一个超人，在城市里助人为乐，打败反派之余，平时过的和蜘蛛侠有一样，还需要打工赚钱。 玩法一开始其实还是挺有意思的，玩家可以控制角色在城市里飞来飞去，加速飞行莽穿大楼，然后完成城市里的各种突发事件，比如熄灭着火的大楼，拯救人质，击败敌人，送平民去医院，帮平民找孩子之类的。 顺带一提，打架战斗的部分比较类似蜘蛛侠，手感还行，防反非常简单，但伤害也不是很高，打敌人的玩法就比较无趣。 完成各种随机事件之后能获得经验，升级之后就能解锁更多超能力。 同时完成任务能提升城市的和平度，但是稍微试了一下，城市和平度降到最低也没啥具体影响，然后完成几个事件又涨回来了。 另外飞行能莽穿大楼一开始看着还挺有意思的，但是当我想试着从楼顶往下莽就发现行不通了，而且建筑上莽出来的洞只是贴图，而且同样的建筑再来一个洞上一个洞的贴图就会消失，让我想要靠莽把建筑损毁的愿望失败了--看来寒霜引擎的破坏效果还真不是小工作室能弄出来的。 除此之外就是玩一些小游戏挣钱了，比如开出租车，去汉堡店打工之类的，挣了钱可以通过手机买衣服，买食品和药物之类的。 有中文，但是机翻。 总体来说是个小品级的超人模拟器，题材和玩法初始都很有趣，可是到了后面就会发现制作组的贫穷真的限制了玩家的游玩体验。 感兴趣的话可以试试。 .[quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

提前声明：[b][i][u]请不要把它当作《超人模拟器》，因为主角并非superman，也称不上是spiderman。[/u][/i][/b] 《Superhero Simulator》省流： +不错的题材[b]切入点[/b] +[b]可破坏[/b]城市建筑 +价格偏低，[b]性价比较高[/b] +[b]海陆空[/b]皆可前往 +[b]画面表现好[/b] -[b]节奏很快[/b] -战斗平庸[b]无趣[/b] -存在不少[b]bug[/b]，例如死亡后会卡在当前页面 -中文疑似[b]机翻[/b]，质量不高 -键盘的个别[b]键位非常奇怪[/b]，且有时不灵敏 接触到这款游戏我第一时间联想到的是21年玩过的一款免费游戏——《[b]UNDEFEATED[/b]》，直译的话就是《不败》，听名字就知道也是款类超人的无敌流游戏。不过该游戏跟本作不同的是，《不败》是真的无敌且是superman，而《Superhero Simulator》更偏向是超能力者的方向，也就是一个拥有非凡能力的人在城市中一边惩恶扬善，一边挣钱交房租的设定。我不好说这两者设定谁高谁低，毕竟这是题材切入点的不同，各有优劣之处。但目前的游玩来看，《Superhero Simulator》在选择了生活+拯救的道路后，其实并没有很好地调整好两方的节奏问题。 首先需要知道的是，本作碍于cuperhero本身是需要交房租的，导致我们前期在解决城市危机后，还得去当滴滴司机，去开一个不限速+无限耐久+超级漂移的出租车，也难为乘客了，这样都不投诉我，还是“满意的客人”😂。 有了生活压力后，我们就要像个普通人一样找工作，而不是像彼得帕克那样还能卖自拍。但是这部分确实有些无趣了，既没有展现出生存压力，也没有刻画出主角在这般情景下非人之处（也许没把乘客颠死也算是个非人之处？）。当然，我们也并非是一直开滴滴，随着流程推进也会跳槽换职业的。 至于卖点的superhero部分，也只能说是差强人意，甚至是普通。 先说战斗，主角的一些招式是随着等级解锁的，但是前期真的太废了，我会飞会冲刺，也能撞穿大楼，但是你打我三枪，我就寄了。而且主角的攻击模组也很少，初期就一个平A，一点都没意思。 但是比较特别的是本作的随机事件还算有趣，例如海上有人落水、城市中有人劫持人质或者是安装炸弹，亦或者有人身患疾病急需送往医院等，较于《不败》是略显丰富的，但是如此内容在中后期也是不够提供有效游玩时长的。 看了下最近的每周公告，似乎本作都会定期更新好看的时装（例如rich man的蝙蝠面具）以及新任务，但是我觉得也许当前先暂缓随机任务的节奏比较好，目前的节奏太快了，这他妈是哪个城市啊，一天好几起炸弹事件，干脆毁灭世界吧bro [code] 点击关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/26214428] 電玩狂熱愛好者 [/url] ，以获取更多游戏评测、资讯、攻略 [/code]

I bought this game with a lot of hope. I read the reviews and saw a high jank factor. But I always have to think back to Rising Star 2. That game is repatitive as hell and is filled with jank. I play it a lot and would say I love it. I looked at this and told myself to expect a similar experience. i bounced after an hour. There is so much potential here, but two things made me curse and uninstall. 1. When I am performing my job I can smash the heck out of anything I want and run over people. This is a very individual thing, but why would I feel like a hero by saving drowing people or physically carrying an injured person to a hospital while my working persona would commit vehicular assault to ensure a happy customer? It really threw me away from the experience. 2. The chase mission. Because of the control scheme of moving based on character viewpoint, I simply could not complete the first villain chase mission. I could not navigate the city streets at speed because I could not control the mouse precisely enough. I tried the keyboard but it was a slower version of using the mouse and I was continuiously disoriented. These are not bad design decisions for everyone. They are bad design decisions for me. I was already halfway out of the door after I blasted my first civilian into lunchmeat with my yellow LTD taxi. The controls walked me out and escorted me to my car. No kiss though. Not on the first date. I will watch the game. I want to see where it goes, and even though I have been playing games for a very long time, I still have hope for EA games working the way we hoped they would; to help independent developers to Iterate, digest feedback, and improve their product.

This game has completely hooked me. I’ve been looking for a true superhero simulator for a long time, and this is the closest anything has come to actually delivering that fantasy. Even in Early Access, the foundation here is genuinely special. The biggest strength of this game is the FEELING. Movement is incredible. Flying feels freeing in a way most superhero games never get right. Super speed, heat vision, thunderclaps, grabbing enemies, and combat all blend into something that actually makes you feel powerful. The city is big enough to support that freedom of movement instead of restricting it, which makes just traversing the world fun on its own. That right there is the core of why this game works: it understands the superhero fantasy. But what makes me excited is not just what’s here — it’s what this game could become. Right now, it already feels like a superhero sandbox. But it has the potential to evolve into a full superhero LIFE simulator. What I’d love to see long-term: First, character creation and identity need even deeper expansion. This game is at its best when you can fully create YOUR hero. I’d love to see more: * Hairstyles, beards, body types, facial variety * More distinct physical diversity in character creation (not just skin tone variation, but actual facial structure differences) * Alien / supernatural / otherworldly appearance options from the start * More customization depth overall Second, power progression could become one of the most important systems in the game. Instead of starting fully powered or quickly becoming OP, I think powers should be part of structured skill trees and identity paths. Examples: * Super strength * Super speed * Telekinesis * Fire / ice / elemental powers * Quantum / energy manipulation * Technopathy * Animal-based or echolocation-type abilities But instead of just choosing them from a menu, I think powers should be tied to STORY AND CHOICE. Your origin should matter. Random or choice-based events could define your path: * Meteor exposure * Experiment gone wrong * Alien inheritance * Magical encounter * Secret academy recruitment * Radioactive/animal bite-type tropes And your decisions in the world (heroic vs selfish vs criminal behavior) could determine what kind of powers you unlock and how your character evolves. That leads into something even bigger: ROLEPLAY IDENTITY. I think the game has massive potential if it leans into choice-based storytelling where you: * Start as a normal person * Work jobs, pay rent, survive * Experience a triggering event that gives you powers * Choose how you respond to those powers * Decide whether you become a hero or a villain That kind of structure would make every playthrough feel different. Traversal should also be expanded beyond just flight and speed. I’d love to see more variety like: * Wall running * Grappling hook traversal * Parkour systems * Gliding * Teleport movement * Swinging mechanics * More grounded “non-flying hero” options Not every superhero fantasy is Superman — some players want Batman, Daredevil, Spider-Man, etc. I also think the city itself could become much more interactive and alive: * Arcades and mini-games * More civilian interactions * More random world events * More interior locations * More activities beyond combat Right now the combat and rescue systems are fun, but the game could become much deeper if the world itself had more things to DO, not just fight. Another big idea is progression and consequence. I think the game would benefit a lot from: * Slower power progression (earning abilities over time) * Meaningful consequences for city damage or failure * Villain pathways with real gameplay differences * A morality system that actually changes how the world reacts to you And long-term, I think there’s even potential for: * Multiplayer/co-op superhero worlds * Team-based hero systems * Multiple cities or even global scale environments * Different origin stories and starting scenarios The reason I’m writing all of this is simple: I’m not criticizing the game because I dislike it — I’m imagining what it could become because the foundation is already strong enough to support something much bigger. Most superhero games never even reach the point where you start thinking like this. But this one does. The core gameplay is already fun enough that it makes you start dreaming about systems, depth, identity, and long-term evolution. That’s rare. The foundation is here. Now it just needs expansion, depth, and continued development. I can’t wait to see where it goes from here.

This game has a lot of potential. I thoroughly enjoy it, but unfortunately in its current state its buggy, repetitive and has very little actual content aside from the hard grind through a hundred levels for mostly cosmetics and power upgrades. I'd very much like to see new powers or power builds to make your own style supe instead of just being a Superman/girl rehash. With only 4 additional suits (after the base four including two holiday style fits), but tons more masks/helmets, I'd like to see more suit variants and cape variants. The basic jobs/careers you do to earn money when you're not super heroing are very minimalistic, but progressively more complicated. Taxi driver, Burger flipper(oddly difficult, the timers are very short) and grocery store simulator (quite literally the same thing but a buggy messy version). Cant put down boxes unless theyre empty, not enough slots for all of the necessary items to run the store, if you dont have something even if you cant afford it the customers get pissy costing you money in the long run. etc. Taxi is the easiest and quickest and for sure the best option to keep gameplay smooth, but adds to repetitiveness. The model for the MC is definitely the model that has received the most love, and your roommate who is your "man in the chair." The NPC's are all AI generated voices and it looks like some of them have AI-generated textures (clothing merging with their skin etc etc.) The Enemy models are fine for the most part. The badguy variance is there, but the combat is very lackluster so they all feel like the same punching bags that either shoot you or try to punch you. The major villains are all pretty much the same, just chasing them down through the city and not even fighting them except for the bosses that repeat every so often, even those boss battles are "Go here, fight multiple groups, damage boss, boss shield/disappears, rinse repeat". So all in all, very blaring issues, but for the actually *good* content like the flight, the (small pool of) powers, the actual superheroing and the really janky funny stuff that happens since its EA, I definitely recommend. I don't think I'm reaching max level before full release, but I am eagerly anticipating what could be for the full release.

This game has a fairly solid foundation. You actively try to balance your personal life and your hero life. On paper its what everyone wants from a hero game. But many aspects of the game are very unpolished. First, combat. It's clunky and downright boring. You start out with just fist attacks, and you don't even get combos. So for a large portion of the beginning of the game, you just mash the attack button on enemies and dodge their attacks. Second, Hero Scenarios. There's actually not much I can critique negatively here. There are a TON of scenarios, from alien invasions to pedestrians needing to go to the hospital, to hostage situations, to finding cats, and so on. There's a TON of these. But it's held back by the clunky and boring combat more than anything. Secondary, too many appear at once, making it impossible to do all of them, mainly because you simply don't fly fast enough. This part needs attention. You take jobs to earn money between saving people. This is a strong concept, also held back by a very barebones foundation. There's four available jobs, though the pizza one could definitely be a fun fifth if its repurposed. The environment itself is okay enough. Its sort of bland because its just a 3D cardboard city with basic traffic/pedestrian AI. It may have sounded negative, but there are a lot of good things here: - funny villains, and a ton of diversity. - tons of hero scenarios, though the game does too many of the same ones. I'd like the developers to implement weights on their scenarios, that slowly decrease the chances of a scenario happening if it has occurred often, rather than a simple RNG pick alone. - More NPC variety. I heard the same phrases over and over again in the taxi job mini-game. And none of them are thankful for your speedy, no collision ride. Overall, the game doesn't take itself seriously at all. While this is charming and amusing (reminds me of Saints Row), I did get sort of bored with the constant comedic approach. I'd like to see some more serious situations. The hero also doesn't maintain a reputation at all, which besides the city peace level, I'd like to see a reputation level on the hero that changes how people feel about you. It's a decent game and it's inexpensive, so I say yes, give it a try.

I approached Superhero Simulator expecting spectacle and found a game that respects systems as much as set dressing. The AI presents smart challenges without restrain. [Overall thoughts ∞ Positive]
Flying above skyscrapers never gets old. The sense of freedom and power makes every mission feel like a dream come true.
I spent an hour just practicing landings. Crashing into cars, lamp posts, and people it’s chaos, but funny chaos.
The city feels alive. Civilians cheer, cops panic, villains taunt it’s like a comic book breathing in 3D.
Combat is fluid. Dodging lasers and countering punches feels cinematic I want every fight to feel like a blockbuster scene.
Rescuing civilians executes with flair. You never feel like you’re just doing chores.
Stealth segments surprised me. Sneaking past radar sensors vs full-on fight gives nice pacing.
Learning combos feels rewarding. Early clunky attacks evolve into graceful power storms.
I love managing hero life and bills. The balance is quirky but meaningful in this open world.
Performance needs tweaks. I dropped settings just to hit smooth framerates. But flying and combat shine.
